sections.h2: Which Cole County offices handle my property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices split the work. The Cole County Assessor values the property, and the Collector of Revenue bills and collects the tax. The Collector's office is in the Courthouse Annex at 311 E High Street, Room 100, Jefferson City, MO 65101, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. at 573-634-9124. A 24 hour drop box sits outside the Annex entrance facing High Street.

The Assessor's page says Cole County has over 33,000 parcels of real estate and more than 30,000 personal property accounts. The Collector handles roughly 94 million dollars in tax revenue, which goes out to the state, several municipalities, rural fire districts, the public library and the county's public school districts. The County Clerk runs the Board of Equalization schedule.

The Missouri State Tax Commission oversees assessors statewide and hears appeals that have already passed through the local board. Questions about a value belong with the Assessor, and questions about a bill or a missing statement belong with the Collector.

sections.h2: When is Cole County property tax due, and what happens if I am late?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is due on receipt of the bill and no later than December 31, with the postmark deciding whether a mailed payment is on time. The Collector mails bills in November. If nothing has arrived by the second week of December, call 573-634-9124, because a missing bill does not excuse the tax or the late fees.

  • Penalties and fees can reach 25% during the first year of delinquency.
  • Delinquent tax is a lien on the property, so a new owner inherits an unpaid balance.
  • Mortgage escrow accounts: if a bill comes to you that your lender pays, forward it to the lender.
  • A seller who still gets a bill after the sale should give the Collector the new owner's name and address.

Payment options include online with a card (2.25% convenience fee), echeck ($1.75 per transaction, allow 5 to 7 days), phone at 855-568-0066, in person, or by mail postmarked by December 31. The drop box accepts payments until midnight on December 31.

sections.h2: How does the Cole County Assessor set the tax amount?
sections.html:
The tax equals assessed value divided by 100, multiplied by the tax rate. The Collector's own example uses $9,500 of assessed value at a rate of $5.1240 for a tax of $486.78. Assessed value is a share of market value: 19% for residential property, 12% for agricultural and 32% for commercial.

Property classAssessment rate
Residential19%
Agricultural12%
Commercial32%

Source: Cole County real estate tax page.

On a house with a market value of $200,000, that 19% rate gives an assessed value of $38,000, and the local levy is then applied to every hundred dollars of it. The rates come from the voters and the taxing districts, and the Assessor's office posts a tax rate sheet. Ask the Assessor or Collector which taxing districts and levy apply to your parcel.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Cole County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with an informal talk with the Assessor, which is optional and can be done between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. Bring evidence of what the home would sell for, such as photographs, an inspection report, a recent appraisal or recent neighborhood sales. The county page reminds owners that the Assessor's job is to see that values reflect current market value.

The next step is the Board of Equalization. By RSMo 137.275, appeals must be lodged by the second Monday in July. The Cole County board has the three County Commissioners, the Assessor as a non-voting member, two appointed members who are not county officers, and two City of Jefferson appointees for properties inside city limits. The County Clerk acts as secretary and mails the written result.

If the board's ruling does not settle it, you may appeal to the State Tax Commission within the time set in the chapter or 30 days after the board's final action, whichever is later (RSMo 138.430). The county page says these hearings are usually held in September and October and are heard by a single Administrative Hearing Officer. A professional appraisal is expected at that level, and an attorney is common but not required.

sections.h2: What happens if Cole County property tax goes unpaid for years?
sections.html:
Land with taxes unpaid for three years can be sold at the delinquent tax certificate sale. The county holds it each year on the fourth Monday in August at 10 a.m. at the Cole County Courthouse, and RSMo 140.150 sets that day statewide. Delinquent tax, penalty, interest and costs can be paid to the Collector at any time before the sale.

  • The list of properties is published in the Jefferson City News Tribune for three straight weeks before the sale.
  • The buyer receives a certificate of purchase, and the original owner can redeem within one year of the sale date.
  • Existing liens are not wiped out by the sale or during redemption.
  • A buyer who does not pay the bid can face a 25% penalty plus a prosecuting attorney fee.

If you are behind and thinking of selling, talk to the Collector first for a payoff figure. The county page says no money is paid to the Collector at the time of a sale. Ask your title company to request any payoff figure in writing.

sections.h2: How does selling a house in Cole County handle this year's tax?
sections.html:
The buyer is responsible for the full bill that arrives in November and must pay it by December 31. Taxes are generally prorated, so the buyer gets a credit at closing for the part of the year you owned the house. The Collector's page explains that no tax payment is made to the Collector at the table.

Cole County is in central Missouri, south of the Missouri River, and covers 402 square miles. Jefferson City is both the county seat and the state capital. Organized on November 16, 1820, the county takes its name from William Temple Cole. Neighbors are Boone, Callaway, Osage, Miller and Moniteau counties. US 50, 54 and 63 and Routes 17 and 179 run through it.

The Census Bureau counts 77,908 residents as of July 1, 2025 and 33,956 housing units. Owners occupy 67.9% of homes, the median home value for 2020 to 2024 is $229,600, and median household income is $74,876. Median gross rent is $834 and the average commute is 17.9 minutes. Building permits numbered 154 in 2025.

School districts that reach the county are Jefferson City Public Schools, Blair Oaks R-II, Cole County R-I at Russellville, Cole County R-V at Eugene and Jamestown C-1. Towns include Jefferson City, Lohman, Russellville, St. Martins, St. Thomas, Taos, Centertown and Wardsville.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to pay property tax in Cole County?
faqs.a: December 31. Payment is due when the bill is received and no later than that date, and mailed payments count by postmark. The drop box at 311 E High Street takes payments until midnight on December 31. Late charges can reach 25% in the first year.

faqs.q: When does Cole County mail property tax bills?
faqs.a: The Collector mails them during November. If you have no bill by the second week of December, call 573-634-9124. A bill that never arrives does not remove the obligation to pay.

faqs.q: What is the last day to file a Board of Equalization appeal in Cole County?
faqs.a: The second Monday in July, filed through the County Clerk's office. Informal talks with the Assessor can happen earlier, and the Assessor's page says the next step after the board is the State Tax Commission.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when a Cole County house sells mid-year?
faqs.a: The buyer pays the full bill by December 31, and taxes are generally prorated so the buyer receives a credit for the months the seller owned the house. No tax is paid to the Collector at closing. A seller who still gets the bill should send the Collector the new owner's address.

faqs.q: How long before a Cole County property is sold for back taxes?
faqs.a: After taxes stay unpaid for three years, the parcel can be offered at the certificate sale held on the fourth Monday in August. The owner can pay the tax, penalty, interest and costs before the sale, or redeem within one year after it.
